title: Facebook Pushes Back Launch Of Smart Speakers Amid Turmoil
text:

Facebook reportedly will begin mass production of the speakers in June, but it has cut order volumes for 2018 by about 20% from its original plan, DigiTimes said. 
Amazon currently leads the smart-speaker market with its lineup of Echo devices, followed by Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google Home devices. 
Apple ( AAPL ) entered the market with its HomePod premium audio speaker in February, but sales have been lackluster, analysts say. Apple has cut production orders for the HomePod to 200,000 units a month from 500,000, DigiTimes said. Facebook Privacy Concerns 
Smart speakers have raised consumer privacy concerns because they are devices in your home that always listen to what you're saying. Smart speakers respond to spoken questions and commands. 
Facebook shares are down as a result of the Cambridge Analytica data-privacy scandal. Zuckerberg testified about the scandal in front of two congressional committees. He apologized to lawmakers for failing to protect user privacy, but defended the company's advertising-based business model. 
Political consultant Cambridge Analytica wrongfully accessed personal data from 87 million Facebook users, which it used during the 2016 presidential election. 
In his testimony, Facebook's Zuckerberg also responded to questions about how the service can prevent hate speech, fake news, propaganda and other undesired content. 
Facebook shares were up 0.5%, near 167.10, in afternoon trading on the stock market today . The stock hit an all-time high of 195.32 on Feb. 1.
